texts.preamble: Imran Khan vs Sualeha Jameel on 27 September, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan Addl. Sessions Judge-02, South-East District Saket Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 123/2025 Ps- Jamia Nagar U/Sec. 29 Pwdv Act In the matter of :- Imran Khan S/o Liyakat Ali R/o 2180, G.F. Katra Mehar Parwar Near Lall Masjid Kuncha Chelan Daryaganj, Delhi- 110002 . .... Appellant Versus Sualeha Jameel D/o Sh. Jameel Ahmad R/o H. No. D-18, 2nd Floor Main Road, Okha Vihar Jamia Nagar, New Delhi- 110025 .... Responden Date of Institution : 15.04.2025 Date of Arguments : 27.09.2025 Date of pronouncement : 27.09.2025 Decision : [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Impugned Order Stand Ca No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Judgment
texts.facts: 1. This is a criminal appeal u/sec 29 of the Protection Protection of woman from Domestic Violence Act 2005 (hereinafter referred to as DV Act) filed by the appellant/ husband namely Imran Khan against the impugned order dated 14.10.2024 (hereinafter referred as 'impugned order') passed by Ld. Trial Court in CT Case No. 1109/2023 titled as "Sualeha Jameel Vs. Imran Khan", vide which appellant/ husband was directed to pay a sum of Rs. 12,044/- per month to the complainant for her maintenance as well as three minor children in her custody, from the date of filing of the application Imran Khan vs Sualeha Jameel on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174504148/ 1 till its disposal. 2. Appellant/ husband herein is the respondent no. 1 and respondent/ wife herein is the complainant before Ld. Trial Court. In order to avoid any confusion, both the parties will be referred with the same nomenclature with which they were referred before Ld. Trial Court, in my subsequent paragraphs. 3. The brief facts necessary for disposal of present appeal as mentioned in appeal are as follows :- "That marriage of the complainant and respondent was solemnized on 10.02.2012 according to the Muslim rites and customs, at Delhi in a lavish manner. Out of the said wedlock, three children were born out who were presently in the custody of complainant. That parents of the complainant have CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 2 of 17 spent huge amount in the said marriage beyond their capacity and as per the demand of the respondent for the happiness of complainant. After the marriage, the complainant was dutiful and never gave any chance of complain but after sometime, the behaviour of respondents have changed towards the complainant and she was being harassed for not bringing the dowry articles as per their whims and also demanded Rs. 15 Lacs and a Car. That all the jewellery articles of complainant were taken by mother-in-law of complainant. Thereafter, due to non- fulfillment of the said demand respondents, abused, beaten, tortured as well as mentally harassed the complainant. That respondent/ husband has extra marital affairs and alcoholic person and upon objection, complainant was beaten by him. It has been stated that respondent/ husband is working as a welder at I.K. Iron Work at Darya Ganj and earning more than Rs. 1,00,000/- per month besides the other source of income. Since, the complainant was subjected to the physical, verbal and emotional abuse as well as the economic abuse committed by the respondents, hence, the present complaint case." And thereafter, matter was fixed for Complainant Evidence. CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 3 of 17 5. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned order dated 14.10.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court, respondent/ husband has challenged the said order by way of present appeal on the following grounds :- a) That impugned order dated 14.10.2024 has been passed without applying the judicial mind and ignoring the true facts and based on the wrong assumption that the appellant is drawing handsome salary. Imran Khan vs Sualeha Jameel on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174504148/ 2 b) That complainant is an over ambitious lady who wants to live a lavish life and soon after the marriage she clarified this fact that appellant/ husband is not to the expectation of the wife and is having a very lower financial status and under the pressure of the society, she had to live with appellant/ husband. But despite that appellant/ husband had always tried to make the complainant understand the hardships of life. c) That no domestic violence of any kind has been inflicted upon the complainant by the appellant/ husband and his family members which amounts to domestic violence. d) That the complainant is brought up in Metro environment and she is unable to adjust herself with appellant/ husband and mere excuses of not fulfilling her marital obligations. e) That appellant/ husband is a poor person having a small earning because he is doing welding job on daily bases at Daryaganj, Tiraha Beram Khan, Delhi, earning Rs. 400/-per day out of which he had to pay rent of Rs. 5000/- per month and also pay Rs. 400/- per month as charges of electricity bills. CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 4 of 17 f) That complainant is well educated lady having Masters Degree from the Jamia Millia University and is doing the job and getting Rs.35,000/- p.m. and also give tuition as tutor to the student at her house from the said tuition she earns not less than Rs.10,000/- pm. g) That granting/ imposing Rs. 12,044/ as interim maintenance to the complainant shall cause financial hardship on the appellant/ husband who will be left with little money to live with. Recently, appellant/ husband father had died and his elderly mother is sitting in IDDAT. Further, recently younger brother of appellant has been diagnosed with brain paralyzed and still he is on bed rest. The appellant bears all the expenses relating to his brother who is on bed since and his elderly mother who is sitting in IDDAT.
texts.arguments: h) That the assumption of the Ld. MM that the appellant is earning more than 1 lakh per month is based on misconception. 6. In addition to the aforesaid grounds, Ld. Counsel for appellant/ husband has argued that Ld. Trial Court has erred in justifying the awarded interim maintenance amount of Rs. 12,044/- per month. The complainant did not disclose her correct income and all the bank account details. She owns a bank account having Account Number 35023280979 with SBI at Zakir Nagar New Delhi branch. It has been argued that since the complainant is financially sound and is earning handsome salary to maintain herself, the maintenance amount awarded vide impugned order, is liable to [LEAKAGE_MASK]. He Imran Khan vs Sualeha Jameel on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174504148/ 3 has relied upon the case law titled as Shiplashree J.M. Vs Gurumanjunatha A.S. 2023 SCC On CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 5 of 17 line Kr 36, decided on 19.06.2023, wherein it has been held that in absence of any explanation suggesting that wife was incapable of working again she is legally bound to meet her own expenses and should only seek supportive maintenance from her husband. 7. Ld. Counsel for appellant/ husband has also relied upon the case law titled as Mamta Jaiswal vs. Rajesh Jaiswal 2000(3) MPLJ 100, wherein it has been observed that Sec. 24 has been enacted for the purpose of providing a monetary assistance to either spouse who is incapable of supporting himself or herself in spite of sincere efforts. However, the law does not expect persons engage in the legal battles to remain idle solely with the objective of squeezing out money from the opposite party. Because it is settled law that a person who approaches the court for granting relief, equitable or otherwise, is under a solemn obligation to candidly & correctly disclose all the materials facts has no right to be heard on the merits of his grievance. Reliance has also been placed upon the case law titled as Megha Khetrapal Vs. Rajat Kapoor, Crl. Rev. P. No. 273/2023 decided on 19.03.2025 by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. It has been prayed that in view of the above, the impugned order dated 14.10.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 8. On other hand, Ld. Counsel for the complainant has argued that the present appeal is devoid of merit and is liable to dismissed. It has been argued that present appeal filed by the appellant/ husband is the blatant abuse of the process of law and instead of making payment of CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 6 of 17 interim maintenance to the complainant and her three minor children, the appellant/ husband has filed present case to avoid the payment to the complainant. That present appeal filed by the appellant is not maintainable as same is filed without any application justifying the delay in filing of present appeal. That appellant/ husband has made contradictory and mutually destructive statements before the Court which shows his lack of bonafide and deliberate attempt to mislead the court. It has been argued that Non-Bailable Warrants were issued against the appellant/ husband by Shri Kuldeep Narayn Ld. Principal Judge Family Court and when police reached to execute the same, the appellant's own brother recorded his statement to the police that appellant was "not living with them" . It has been argued that if the appellant was genuinely disowned and not living with his family, there can be no question of him having financial liabilities towards them. It has been argued that appellant has clearly shifted his stand as per his convenience claiming "disownment" earlier to avoid disclosure of assets and income and now citing "family liabilities" to seek reduction in his maintenance obligation and to avoid his responsibilities against his first priorities i.e. his wife and three minor children. It has been argued that in Dalip Singh v. State of U.P., (2010) 2 SCC 114 , Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that a litigant who withholds material facts or makes misleading statements is not entitled to any relief. Applying this principle, the appellant's appeal deserves to be dismissed at the threshold. It has been argued that plea of financial incapacity is false and self-serving. Even if taken at face value, the appellant's obligation to maintain his wife and three children is statutory and cannot be CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 7 of 17 evaded, as reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena, (2015) 6 SCC 353". It has been argued that the grounds of appeal are vague and present appeal is liable to be dismissed. 10. Section 20 of the DV Act stipulates that a Magistrate hearing an application under Section 12 of the DV Act may direct Respondent to pay certain monetary relief to the aggrieved person. It further delineates the contours of monetary relief that is to be paid to aggrieved person, including the criteria governing it as well as the manner in which the payment is to be made. For the ease of comprehension, Section 20 of the DV Act has been reproduced as under :- "20. Monetary reliefs (1)While disposing of an application under sub-section (1) of section 12, the Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence and such relief may include, but not limited to, (a)the loss of earnings; (b)the medical expenses; (c)the loss caused due to the destruction, damage or removal of any property from the control of the aggrieved person; and CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 8 of 17 (d)the maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as her children, if any, including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance under section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) or any other law for the time being in force. (2)The monetary relief granted under this section shall be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed." 11. 12. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household. According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence. Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act. 14. For computing the maintenance, the following test have been laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Jasbir Kaur Sehgal vs. District Judge, Dehradun & Ors. 1997 (7) SCC 7, wherein it has been observed that: "No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. Some scope for leverage can, however, be always there. The court has to consider the status of parties, their respective needs, the capacity of husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions. The amount of maintenance fixed for wife or children should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate." Imran Khan vs Sualeha Jameel on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174504148/ 6 CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 11 of 17 15. Further, Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr, Crl. Appeal No. 730/2020 (arising out of SLP (Crl) No. 9503/2018, dated 04.11.2020 has held as under :- Criteria for determining quantum of maintenance :- The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance to be awarded. The factors which would weigh with the Court inter alia are the status of the parties; reasonable needs of the wife and dependent children; whether the applicant is educated and professionally qualified; whether the applicant has any independent source of income; whether the income is sufficient to enable her to maintain the same standard of living as she was accustomed to in her matrimonial home; whether the applicant was employed prior to her marriage; whether she was working during the subsistence of the marriage; whether the wife was required to sacrifice her employment opportunities for nurturing the family, child rearing, and looking after adult members of the family; reasonable costs of litigation for a nonworking wife. 16. Besides that, the court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or her child or his support, the financial capacity of the husband, his actual income, reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and dependent family members including his own child, whom he is obliged to maintain under the law, liabilities if any, would be required to be taken into CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 12 of 17 consideration. The Court must have due regard to the standard of living of the husband, as well as the spiraling inflation rates and high costs of living. The plea of the husband that he does not possess any such source of income through which, he could maintain her wife, ipso facto does not absolve him of his moral duty to maintain his wife or his child if he is able bodied and has educational qualifications. Under section 20 DV Act, the magistrate has powers to direct husband to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence and such relief may inter alia include the maintenance for aggrieved person as well as her children. 18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case law titled as Dr. Kulbhushan Kunwar v. Raj Kumari (1970) 3 SCC 129, has held, which as under :- "12. Section 125 Cr.P.C. stipulates that if any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain his wife, his legitimate or illegitimate minor child, who are otherwise unable to maintain themselves, shall be obligated to do so. A moral duty and a statutory obligation is cast upon the husband to maintain his wife, minor Imran Khan vs Sualeha Jameel on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174504148/ 7 children, parents who otherwise are not capable of maintaining themselves. CA No. 123/2025 Imran Khan Vs. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 13 of 17 19. The paternity of the children are also not in dispute. Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr (Supra) has held as under :- (c) Where wife is earning some income. The Courts have held that if the wife is earning, it cannot operate as a bar from being awarded maintenance by the husband. The Courts have provided guidance on this issue in the following judgments. 23. Further, in order to determine the quantum of maintenance payable to an applicant, the Court shall take into account the criteria enumerated in Part B - III of the judgment Rajnesh Vs Neha and Anr. (supra). The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. 24. It is a settled position of law that at the stage of granting interim maintenance, the Court has to take a prima facie view based on the pleadings and material available on record. The burden to prove that wife is gainfully employed and having sufficient independent income lies upon the husband. Sualeha Jameel Page no. 15 of 17 25.
